From 702d1e81feae70aa16ca364b4d2d95ccad801022 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Terry Zhou <bjzhou@marvell.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2018 10:44:05 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] pinctrl: armada-37xx: Fix spurious irq management

Until now, if we found spurious irq in irq_handler, we only updated the
status in register but not the status in the code. Due to this the system
will got stuck dues to the infinite loop

[gregory.clement@bootlin.com: update comment and add fix and stable tags]
Fixes: 30ac0d3b0702 ("pinctrl: armada-37xx: Add edge both type gpio irq support")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Terry Zhou <bjzhou@marvell.com>
Reviewed-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c b/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
index 0f1eafba0ded..674ffdf8103c 100644
--- a/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
+++ b/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
@@ -666,12 +666,13 @@ static void armada_37xx_irq_handler(struct irq_desc *desc)
 					writel(1 << hwirq,
 					       info->base +
 					       IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
-					continue;
+					goto update_status;
 				}
 			}
 
 			generic_handle_irq(virq);
 
+update_status:
 			/* Update status in case a new IRQ appears */
 			spin_lock_irqsave(&info->irq_lock, flags);
 			status = readl_relaxed(info->base +
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c`**
   - The line that previously contained `continue;` within the `armada_37xx_irq_handler` function has been replaced with a `goto update_status;` statement. 
   - This change ensures that when a spurious IRQ is detected, the code will jump to the `update_status` label, allowing the status to be updated correctly in the code, rather than just in the register.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where the system could get stuck in an infinite loop due to improper handling of spurious IRQs. By changing the flow of control from `continue;` to `goto update_status;`, the patch ensures that the IRQ status is updated in the code, which is crucial for proper IRQ management. This change is directly related to the previously identified issue in the IRQ handling logic, as noted in the commit message and the Fixes tag.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
status = readl_relaxed(info->base + IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
status &= readl_relaxed(info->base + IRQ_EN + 4 * i);
```
Reason:
These statements read the current IRQ status and filter it based on the enabled interrupts. However, when a spurious IRQ is detected, the handler only acknowledges the IRQ without updating the status in the code, leading to an infinite loop as the same spurious IRQ is processed repeatedly without exiting.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
goto update_status;
```
```c
status = readl_relaxed(info->base + IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
```
Reason:
The addition of the `goto update_status;` statement ensures that after handling a spurious IRQ, the status is updated correctly before the next iteration. This prevents the infinite loop by ensuring that the IRQ status is re-evaluated, allowing the handler to exit if no further interrupts are present.
